topics.title: Binary Search on Answer & Search Space Reduction
topics.summary: Master the 'Binary Search on Answer' paradigm for min-max optimization problems.
topics.interviewTip: Use (pile + speed - 1) / speed for ceiling division — avoids floating point. Key insight: identify what to binary-search (the answer, not the index).

topics.title: Sliding Window: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
topics.summary: O(N) sliding window with character index map and dynamic left pointer adjustment.
topics.interviewTip: int[128] array is 10x faster than HashMap<Character, Integer> due to no boxing. Always clarify if input is ASCII, extended ASCII, or Unicode.

references.title: LeetCode 3: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters

topics.title: Topological Sort & Cycle Detection in Directed Graphs
topics.summary: Kahn's BFS algorithm for dependency ordering and cycle detection in DAGs.
topics.interviewTip: Kahn's detects cycles naturally — if output length < V, there's a cycle. Prefer Kahn's for counting/ordering; DFS coloring for just cycle detection.

topics.title: Dijkstra's Shortest Path Algorithm with PriorityQueue
topics.summary: Single-source shortest path in weighted non-negative graphs using a min-heap.
topics.interviewTip: Dijkstra fails with negative edges — the greedy assumption breaks. Always ask if weights can be negative. The 'stale entry' skip (d > dist[u]) avoids O(V²) by not using a visited array.

topics.title: 0/1 Knapsack & Subset Sum Space Optimization
topics.summary: 0/1 Knapsack: 2D table → 1D rolling array via reverse iteration.
topics.interviewTip: Reverse iteration converts 2D DP to 1D because dp[c - wt[i]] still refers to the previous item's row (not yet overwritten). Forward iteration = unbounded (Coin Change).

topics.title: Longest Common Subsequence (LCS) & String DP
topics.summary: 2D string DP for LCS, Edit Distance, and sequence diffing.
topics.interviewTip: LCS and Edit Distance use the same 2D table structure. For Edit Distance: dp[i-1][j-1] = replace, dp[i-1][j] = delete, dp[i][j-1] = insert.

topics.title: Two Pointers: Container With Most Water & 3Sum
topics.summary: Reduce O(n²) brute force to O(n) using left/right pointer convergence on sorted arrays.
topics.interviewTip: Two pointers only work on SORTED arrays. In 3Sum, skip duplicate values at both the anchor (i) and inner pointers to avoid duplicate triplets.

topics.title: Fast & Slow Pointers: Floyd's Cycle Detection
topics.summary: Detect cycles in linked lists/arrays using slow (1x) and fast (2x) pointer technique.
topics.interviewTip: When slow and fast meet inside cycle, the distance from head to cycle-start equals distance from meeting point to cycle-start. This is the mathematical basis of Phase 2.

topics.title: Linked List: Reverse, Merge Sorted & Find Middle
topics.summary: Core linked list operations: iterative reverse, merge two sorted lists, and middle node.
topics.interviewTip: Three-pointer reverse: remember prev → cur → next. Draw 3 nodes on whiteboard. Common mistake: losing next pointer before reassigning cur.next.

topics.title: Linked List: Remove Nth from End, Palindrome Check
topics.summary: Remove Nth node from end in one pass; palindrome check by reversing second half.
topics.interviewTip: For 'Remove Nth from end': use dummy node so you can delete the head without special case. Advance fast pointer n+1 times (not n) so slow lands one node before target.

references.title: LeetCode 19: Remove Nth Node From End of List

topics.title: Stack: Valid Parentheses, Min Stack & Daily Temperatures
topics.summary: Classic stack problems: bracket matching, O(1) min-tracking, and monotonic stack intro.
topics.interviewTip: Always use ArrayDeque instead of Stack in Java — Stack extends Vector (synchronized, legacy). ArrayDeque is O(1) for push/pop with no synchronization overhead.

topics.title: Monotonic Stack: Next Greater Element & Largest Rectangle
topics.summary: Monotonic decreasing/increasing stack for next-greater and largest-rectangle problems.
topics.interviewTip: Append a sentinel 0 at the end of heights array to flush the stack cleanly. For circular arrays (Next Greater Element II), iterate 2×N and use index % N.

topics.title: Queue & Sliding Window Maximum (Deque O(n))
topics.summary: O(n) sliding window maximum using a monotonic deque instead of O(n²) brute force.
topics.interviewTip: The deque stores indices (not values) so you can check if front index is outside the window. dq.peekFirst() always gives the index of the current window maximum.

topics.title: Binary Tree Traversals: Inorder, Preorder, Postorder, Level Order
topics.summary: All four traversals implemented recursively and iteratively in Java.
topics.interviewTip: Iterative inorder is the most common follow-up — push left spine onto stack, pop and visit, then go right. Memorize this pattern cold.

topics.title: Binary Tree: Max Depth, Diameter, Path Sum & LCA
topics.summary: High-frequency tree DFS problems: depth, diameter, path sum, and lowest common ancestor.
topics.interviewTip: Diameter uses a global variable — the diameter may not pass through the root. LCA: if both left and right return non-null, current node is the LCA.

topics.title: BST: Validate, Kth Smallest & Lowest Common Ancestor
topics.summary: Exploit BST's inorder-sorted property for validation, search, and LCA in O(h) time.
topics.interviewTip: Common mistake: checking only immediate parent instead of using range bounds for validation. Pass (min, max) bounds down — left child updates max, right child updates min.

topics.title: Graph BFS: Shortest Path, Rotting Oranges & Word Ladder
topics.summary: BFS guarantees shortest path in unweighted graphs — template for grid and word problems.
topics.interviewTip: BFS = shortest path in UNWEIGHTED graphs. Multi-source BFS (Rotting Oranges, 01 Matrix) — add all sources to queue at level 0, then run standard BFS.

topics.title: Union-Find (DSU): Connected Components & Redundant Connection
topics.summary: Disjoint Set Union with path compression and union by rank for near-O(1) component operations.
topics.interviewTip: Path compression alone makes find O(log n). Combined with union by rank, it's O(α(n)) ≈ O(1) practically. union() returns false = cycle detected.

topics.title: Heap & Priority Queue: Kth Largest & Merge K Sorted Lists
topics.summary: Min-heap and max-heap patterns for Kth largest, Top K frequent, and K-way merge.
topics.interviewTip: For Kth largest: use MIN-heap of size K (counterintuitive — the min of the top K elements IS the Kth largest). Bucket sort alternative: O(n) time when values range is bounded.

topics.title: Two Heaps Pattern: Median of Data Stream
topics.summary: Maintain two heaps (max-heap + min-heap) to find median in O(log n) per insert.
topics.interviewTip: Always push to maxHeap first, then rebalance to minHeap — this ensures the ordering invariant is maintained without conditional logic.

references.title: LeetCode 295: Find Median from Data Stream

topics.title: HashMap Patterns: Two Sum, Subarray Sum & Group Anagrams
topics.summary: Core hashmap interview patterns: complement lookup, prefix sum counting, and string grouping.
topics.interviewTip: Prefix sum + HashMap is the key pattern for subarray problems with a target sum. Seed the map with {0:1} to handle subarrays starting from index 0.

topics.title: Recursion & Memoization: From Exponential to Linear
topics.summary: Understand recursion call stacks, memoization, and the top-down DP approach.
topics.interviewTip: Interviewers expect you to start with recursive solution, identify overlapping subproblems, add memoization, then suggest bottom-up DP. Show this progression clearly.

topics.title: Backtracking: Subsets, Permutations & Combination Sum
topics.summary: Universal backtracking template for Subsets, Permutations, Combinations, and N-Queens.
topics.interviewTip: Backtracking time complexity is O(N! or 2^N × N) — always mention this. The `start` index prevents reuse in Subsets/Combinations; remove it for Permutations (use `visited` array instead).

topics.title: Merge Sort & Quick Sort: Implementation & Analysis
topics.summary: Implement Merge Sort (stable O(n log n)) and Quick Sort (in-place, average O(n log n)).
topics.interviewTip: Java uses Dual-Pivot QuickSort for primitives (Arrays.sort) and TimSort for objects (Collections.sort, which is stable). Quick Sort worst case is avoided with random pivot or median-of-three.

topics.title: Trie (Prefix Tree): Insert, Search & Word Search II
topics.summary: Trie for O(L) prefix search, autocomplete, and multi-word matrix search.
topics.interviewTip: In Word Search II, store the full word string at leaf nodes (instead of reconstructing via path) and set node.word = null after finding it to avoid duplicates.

topics.title: DP: Climbing Stairs, House Robber & Jump Game
topics.summary: Foundation DP patterns: linear recurrence and decision at each index.
topics.interviewTip: House Robber II: circular array trick — run House Robber twice (exclude first element, exclude last element) and take the max. Space-optimize to O(1) with two variables.

topics.title: DP: Coin Change & Unbounded Knapsack
topics.summary: Minimum coins (Coin Change) and number of combinations — forward iteration for unbounded reuse.
topics.interviewTip: Forward vs backward iteration is the core insight: forward (unbounded — can reuse), backward (0/1 — use each once). Outer loop on coins for combinations, outer loop on amounts for permutations.

topics.title: DP: Longest Increasing Subsequence (LIS) — O(n log n)
topics.summary: LIS in O(n²) DP and O(n log n) patience sorting with binary search.
topics.interviewTip: tails[i] = smallest tail element of all IS of length i+1. The array stays sorted, enabling binary search. tails.size() = LIS length (tails itself is NOT necessarily the LIS).

topics.title: Bit Manipulation: XOR Tricks, Count Set Bits & Power of 2
topics.summary: XOR for finding unique numbers, Brian Kernighan's algorithm, and common bitwise patterns.
topics.interviewTip: n & (n-1) clears the lowest set bit — this makes counting set bits O(k) where k = number of set bits, not O(32). XOR self-cancellation is the single-number trick.

topics.title: Greedy Algorithms: Activity Selection, Jump Game & Gas Station
topics.summary: When greedy works: optimal substructure + greedy choice property. Key interval and circuit problems.
topics.interviewTip: For interval problems, sorting by END time is usually the greedy key (not start time). Gas Station: if total gas >= total cost, a solution always exists. The valid start is where tank last reset to 0.
